acceptedFindings.title: Cumulative incidence estimates reported without any measure of uncertainty
evidenceRefs: stats-run/stats-run.json (estimates array lacks confidence intervals or standard errors)
stats-run/stats-qa.json (check 'uncertainty-and-pvalue-context' warns only about p-value interpretation, no actual intervals)
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without confidence intervals, readers cannot assess the precision of the point estimates, making the comparison between groups scientifically and clinically unreliable.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Compute and report 95% confidence intervals using resampling or asymptotic methods for the Aalen-Johansen estimator, and include them in all tables and figures.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: stats-run.json contains no fields for lower/upper confidence bounds; the estimates.csv artifact (not inspected) may contain columns for confidence, but the manuscript does not reference them.

acceptedFindings.title: Unbound exploratory analysis precludes confirmatory interpretation
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The analysis lacks a pre-specified protocol or analysis plan. All findings must be considered exploratory and cannot support causal or clinical conclusions. Any claim beyond description of this specific dataset is unsafe.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Either bind the run to a pre-registered analysis specification or clearly label the entire manuscript as exploratory data analysis with no inferential claims. Remove any language suggesting generalization.

acceptedFindings.title: Cumulative incidence time horizon not defined
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Cumulative incidence is a function of time; reporting a 'final' value without specifying the follow-up time is clinically meaningless and could be severely misleading (e.g., inflating risk due to longer follow-up in one group).
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Specify the time point(s) at which cumulative incidence is reported (e.g., 1 year, 5 years) and, if reporting the maximum observed time, explicitly justify its clinical relevance and present the distribution of follow-up times per group.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: The manuscript states 'final cumulative incidence' without any time unit or justification; the stats-run.json estimates object has no 'time' or 'endpoint' key.

acceptedFindings.title: Study question, exposure, event of interest, and competing events not defined
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md (no definition of treatment arms or event codes)
stats-run/stats-run.json (variables list includes 'treatment', 'competing_event', but no dictionary)
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without a clear definition, the entire analysis is unmoored from any clinical context, making it impossible for a reader to evaluate appropriateness, applicability, or even basic meaning.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Explicitly state the research question, define each variable including coding (e.g., 0/1 for treatment, event types), and describe the population from which the data were drawn.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: The manuscript abstract claims a 'prespecified study question' but never states it; the methods section only lists variable names without meaning.

acceptedFindings.title: Analysis lacks binding to a prespecified protocol (unbound/exploratory)
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Unplanned analyses increase the risk of selective reporting and cannot support confirmatory conclusions. While the manuscript caveats this, the presentation of point estimates without uncertainty still invites overinterpretation.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Either restrict all claims to pure exploration (no numeric reporting) or initiate a formal protocol with an AnalysisSpec, method-selection evidence, and rerun the analysis under that bound plan before any dissemination.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: stats-run.json binding.status is 'unbound'; stats-qa warnings confirm.

acceptedFindings.title: Incomplete reporting of missing data and potential selection bias
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md (mentions missingness as limitation but provides no details)
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Complete-case analysis can introduce bias if data are not missing completely at random. Without information on the extent and pattern of missingness, the validity of the 240 records is not assured.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report original sample size, number and proportion of missing values per variable, explore missingness mechanisms, and perform a sensitivity analysis (e.g., multiple imputation) or justify the MCAR assumption.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: The artifacts contain no missingness report or description of dropped records.

acceptedFindings.title: Missing cohort description and variable definitions
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The manuscript does not describe the study population, inclusion/exclusion criteria, event types, censoring, or the meaning of the treatment variable levels (0 and 1). Without this information, the study context is lost, and results cannot be evaluated.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add a detailed cohort and variable description, including definitions of survival_time, competing_event, treatment, and the event-of-interest coding. Specify how censoring and competing events were handled.

acceptedFindings.title: No confidence intervals or uncertainty measures reported
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Cumulative incidence estimates are reported as point estimates only. Readers cannot assess the precision or statistical significance. This severely limits interpretability.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report 95% confidence intervals for the cumulative incidence estimates at specified time points, or provide the variance-covariance matrix. If the Aalen-Johansen implementation does not provide them, use bootstrap or alternative methods.

acceptedFindings.title: Ambiguous time horizon for 'final cumulative incidence'
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: It is unclear whether the 'final cumulative incidence' refers to the maximum observed time, which can vary between groups and be unstable. Cumulative incidence functions should be reported at clinically meaningful or fixed time points.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Define time points of interest (e.g., 1 year, 5 years) and report cumulative incidence at those points with confidence intervals. Provide the full cumulative incidence curves as a figure (already exists).

acceptedFindings.title: Statistical method not explicitly justified or described
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The manuscript says the method was 'inferred from artifacts' but does not name the specific method (Aalen-Johansen) or justify why it was chosen over other competing risk approaches (e.g., Fine-Gray, cause-specific hazards). This hinders understanding and reproducibility.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Explicitly state the statistical method and provide a brief justification, including why the competing risks framework was needed, and reference the specific estimator and its assumptions (e.g., non-informative censoring).

acceptedFindings.title: Results not connected to any prespecified study question
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The manuscript's introduction asks 'What does the analyzed dataset show for the prespecified study question?' but no prespecified question is stated. The analysis appears to be a post-hoc exploration without a clearly defined hypothesis or objective, making it unclear what the findings mean.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: State the prespecified study question clearly in the introduction. If no question was prespecified, frame the analysis as exploratory and limit conclusions accordingly.

acceptedFindings.title: No covariate adjustment or baseline balance assessment
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md (methods list covariates but none used)
stats-run/stats-run.json (only three variables, none beyond time/event/treatment)
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: In an observational dataset, unadjusted comparisons of CIF between treatment groups may be confounded by baseline characteristics. The manuscript does not address this potential source of bias.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: If the study aims to compare groups, present baseline characteristics by group and either adjust (e.g., via Fine-Gray model with covariates) or explicitly note that the analysis is purely descriptive and should not be used for causal inference.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: No model output or balance table exists in the artifacts.

acceptedFindings.title: Manuscript content is skeletal and largely boilerplate
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The results section contains only two bullet points with no descriptive statistics (sample size per group, number of events, follow-up duration, competing events count), precluding any substantive interpretation.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Revise the manuscript to include a table of baseline characteristics, numbers at risk, event counts per group, median follow-up, and a clear description of the CIF curves (figure). Follow STROBE or relevant reporting guidelines.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Word count of 'Results' section is minimal; no numeric details beyond the two incidences.

acceptedFindings.title: No analytic code provided
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: While the run directory contains outputs, there is no code listing showing the exact procedure used to generate the estimates. Reproducibility is limited if the raw data and code are not available.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Include the R or Python script (or equivalent) that produced the Aalen-Johansen estimates, along with any data preprocessing steps, to enable full independent replication.

acceptedFindings.title: No evaluation of censoring or competing risk assumptions
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The Aalen-Johansen estimator assumes non-informative censoring and correct specification of competing events. There is no assessment of follow-up completeness, loss to follow-up, or other potential informative censoring.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report summary statistics on follow-up time, number of events (of each type), and number censored. Discuss any potential informative censoring and sensitivity analyses if feasible.
